report.summary: Evaluated correctness.py chunk 10: function signature, docstring, and body up to line ~1130. Verified docstring claims against visible code; noted risks about freeze_selection and reference_patch calls.
risks: line 1082 | high | use_reference parameter default False, but docstring says it evaluates task's own fix commit. If caller expects True but passes nothing, behavior differs. | Check all call sites to confirm default is appropriate.

line 1109 | medium | freeze_selection called before worktree exists; docstring claims it freezes selection. If freeze_selection modifies global state or has side effects, risk of inconsistency. | Review freeze_selection implementation for side effects.
line 1136 | medium | reference_patch called with exclude=selection.test_overlay; if overlay paths are incorrect, patch may be wrong. | Verify overlay exclusion logic in reference_patch.
line 1149 | low | Exception catch-all (noqa BLE001) may mask unexpected errors; docstring says 'reported, never raised' but no logging visible. | Add logging or re-raise for unexpected exceptions.

handoff.purpose: Define evaluate_correctness function with docstring, validation, worktree setup, before/after measurement.

symbols.name: evaluate_correctness
symbols.note: Evaluates one change against one task using a disposable worktree.

claims.why: All early returns (finish) and the outer try/except catch Exception return finish(...). No raise in visible code.

claims.text: The whole measurement happens in ONE disposable worktree, in this order: FREEZE the selection -> checkout base -> overlay tests -> RUN BEFORE -> judge the TASK -> apply the change -> RUN AFTER -> judge the CHANGE
claims.why: Code shows: freeze_selection (line 1109), disposable_worktree (line 1112), apply_test_overlay (1115-1119), _run_lists before (1122), judge_before_state (1124-1125), apply_patch (1141-1142), _run_lists after (1145). Order matches.

claims.text: The selection is frozen FIRST, before the worktree exists and long before any candidate bytes are applied, and the after-state is run against that same frozen object -- so the thing being measured cannot be influenced by the thing being measured. The frozen declaration and its digest travel on the result.
claims.why: freeze_selection called at line 1109 before disposable_worktree (1112). After run (1145) uses same selection variable. Result includes selection (line 1099).

claims.text: The before-state is measured every time, in the same tree the after-state is measured in. It is never read from a stored receipt here, because a receipt is a claim about a tree that may no longer exist -- the same doctrine ``spine.bootstrap`` applies to its discrimination receipt.
claims.why: No reference to spine.bootstrap or stored receipts in this chunk. The before measurement is done (lines 1122-1125) but claim about doctrine is outside scope.

claims.text: ``use_reference`` evaluates the task's OWN fix commit (``reference_revision``) instead of a candidate patch. That is how a corpus task is validated: a task whose own reference patch does not produce ``fixed`` is not a task.
claims.why: Code: if use_reference: change_bytes = reference_patch(root, base, task['reference_revision'], ...) (lines 1135-1138). else: change_bytes = patch_bytes (line 1140).

claims.text: FROZEN HERE -- before the worktree exists, before the overlay, and long before any candidate bytes are applied. Everything below reads this object; nothing below reads `task` for a node id again.
claims.why: freeze_selection called at line 1109. After that, task is not dereferenced for node ids (only task['reference_revision'] at 1137 and task['repo'] at 1104, but those are before freeze). The selection object is used for all runs.

claims.text: REPORTED as invalid, never silently dropped and never counted as a pass -- the same rule mint.py applies to a vacuous label.
claims.why: Comment refers to mint.py rule; not present in this chunk. The code does return finish(OUTCOME_TASK_INVALID, ...) (line 1130).

claims.text: SAME frozen selection, deliberately: the after run measures exactly what was declared before the change existed.
claims.why: After run (line 1145) uses same 'selection' variable as before run (line 1122). No reassignment of selection between.

observations.what: Function returns CorrectnessResult with 'change' field set to 'reference' if use_reference, else 'patch' if patch_bytes is not None, else None.
validate_task is called but not defined in this chunk; if it raises instead of returning problems, the docstring claim 'never raises' could be broken.
freeze_selection is called with timeout_s parameter; docstring does not mention timeout.
apply_test_overlay is called with selection.test_overlay; if overlay is None or empty, it may raise? Code catches FileNotFoundError, OverlayEscape, OSError.

after _run_lists (line 1145) is inside try/except that catches Exception, but the before run (line 1122) is not in a try block for that same exception scope; if _run_lists raises, it propagates to outer except at line 1148.
